title: A verified disaster-food replacement route can restore a bounded benefit without proving food-security recovery
source_unit: Connecticut DSS SNAP replacement route after July 2026 storm power outages
geography: Connecticut SNAP households affected by the July 4, 2026 storm

denominator.unit: Connecticut SNAP households with at least four hours of storm-related power loss; eligible population count not disclosed

exposure.value: Food purchased with SNAP benefits may have been destroyed after a storm-related power outage lasting at least four hours

report_deadline.unit: deadline to report food loss to DSS

verification.value: DSS must obtain a signed household statement and verify the outage and destruction through collateral contact, utility documentation, community agency documentation, or a home visit

replacement_cap.value: Replacement benefits equal the verified loss up to the household's monthly SNAP benefit amount

issuance_timing.value: Within ten days after the loss report or within two working days after the required signed statement, whichever is later

observations.method: Structured extraction from the official Connecticut Governor and DSS announcement; exposure, report deadline, verification, cap, and issuance timing are retained as separate stages.
observations.uncertainty: The public announcement does not disclose claims filed, claims approved, replacement dollars issued, actual receipt, replacement adequacy, subsequent food security, debt, trust, or household recovery.
observations.subgroup: Connecticut SNAP recipients with qualifying July 4 storm power outages and spoiled SNAP-purchased food; no complete eligible-household denominator is supplied.
observations.counterinterpretation: A defined verification and issuance route can make a disaster remedy reachable in principle, but a deadline, cap, and processing rule do not establish that households reported, qualified, received, or found the replacement adequate.

related_sources.claim: Connecticut distinguishes replacement of food destroyed by a qualifying household disaster from nonreplacement of electronically stolen benefits.

boundary: This record establishes a named storm exposure and an official report-verification-replacement route with a cap and timing rule. It does not establish claim uptake, approved or received replacements, adequacy, food security, trust, or durable household recovery.
